title: The Fine day for the walk
subtitle: 仪表穿着 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 仪表穿着（人与自我·生活与学习·个人仪表与穿着）
meta: 主题语境：仪表穿着（人与自我·生活与学习·个人仪表与穿着）　|　核心词汇：fine　|　正文 339 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 fine 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1958 the engineer wrote of ① a fine day for the walk in the manual, and everybody in the workshop said at once that it was ② finer than the one named there the year before. Three years on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the engineer, who never explained anything, had done it year after year and gone home; it was the fine ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the finest day for the walk anybody in the workshop had ever seen, or so the manual for April 1952 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too fine to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the worker who had come to help; the fine ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the lever at the far bench, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a fine cloth from the town, and said that no worker in his right mind would call it ⑥ as fine as the cloth from the town they had once had in the old workshop. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was fine or not, and he said so.

By 1965 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the manual. What the line asked for was ⑦ something fine, and nothing besides. The worker from the next workshop called the whole plan ⑧ quite fine; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the manual kept the names of the fine ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1968, for the whole place, she wrote of another fine day for the walk in the same manual, and the work, which took two years, seemed ⑨ finer than anybody had expected. ⑩ The finest cloth from the town in the whole workshop, she said in 1970, was the one she could never quite name; the fine ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 好（前置定语 a fine day for the walk：1958 年工程师在说明书里记下的那件好的天气）
B. adj. 好／精美（比较级 finer than：文中两处，一处比适合散步的好天气，一处比预想）
C. adj. 好／精美（最高级 the finest：文中两处，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 好（表语 too fine to do：母亲觉得它太好，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 精美（前置定语 a fine cloth from the town：叔叔把整件事称作一桩精美的细布）
F. adj. 精美（同级比较 as fine as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩城里的细布相比）
G. adj. 精美（后置定语 something fine：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 精美（受程度副词修饰 quite fine：那位工人的评价）

items.q: a fine day for the walk
the finest day for the walk anybody
a fine cloth from the town
The finest cloth from the town in

answers.why: fine 意为“好”，1958 年工程师在说明书里记下的是“一件好的天气”，此处作前置定语 a fine day for the walk。
fine 意为“好”，此处用比较级 finer than，拿它跟前一年记下的那一个相比。
fine 意为“好”，说明书上 四月 那行字说它是车间里最好的一件，故用最高级 the finest day for the walk。
fine 意为“好”，母亲认为这件东西“太好了，谁也用不上”，too fine to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
fine 意为“精美”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩精美的细布”，此处作前置定语 a fine cloth from the town。
fine 意为“精美”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩城里的细布一样精美”，同级比较用 as fine as。
fine 意为“精美”，说明书上那半行字要的是“精美的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something fine。
fine 意为“精美”，邻车间来的那位工人认为这套计划“相当精美”，quite 修饰原级 fine。
fine 意为“精美”，1968 年那趟活儿“比任何人预想的都要精美”，故用比较级 finer than。
fine 意为“精美”，母亲 1970 年说的是“整个车间里最精美的那一桩”，故用最高级 the finest cloth from the town。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1958 年，工程师在说明书里记下了一件好的天气。（a fine day for the walk）
人人都说它比前一年记下的那一个更好。（finer than …）
母亲觉得它太好，谁也用不上。（too fine to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩精美的细布。（a fine cloth from the town）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩城里的细布一样精美。（as fine as …）
到了 1965 年，说明书上只剩半行字：要的是一件精美的东西。（something fine）
answers: In 1958 the engineer wrote of a fine day for the walk in the manual.
Everybody said it was finer than the one named there the year before.
My mother thought it too fine to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a fine cloth from the town.
He said nobody would call it as fine as the cloth from the town they had once had.
By 1965 the manual asked for nothing but something fine.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 fine 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1958 the engineer wrote of a fine day for the walk in the manual, and nobody forgot it.
It was the finest day for the walk in the workshop, or so the manual says.
My mother thought it too fine to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a fine cloth from the town, and nobody argued with him.
The worker from the next workshop called the plan quite fine, and everybody laughed.
The fine ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
